messages:
olivia: Heads up — after the midnight SSO config push some org admins are being dropped to guest and can't access the dashboard. Happening to people who sign in via SAML.
alex: saw this too. quick grep of auth logs shows a bunch of attribute decryption errors around 02:03 UTC.
sre_oncall: log snippet: 
```
2026-02-14T02:03:19Z auth-service ERROR attr-decrypt failed tenant=redwood key=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:alias/sso-key error=kms:DecryptTimeout
2026-02-14T02:03:19Z auth-service WARN missing attribute department for user=alice@example.com, applying default role=guest
```

olivia: that's the flow. we switched to encrypting department with KMS envelope keys as part of the SAML hardening PR (PR #4821). JIT provisioning expects `department` or `eduPersonScopedAffiliation` to map admin roles. If decrypt fails, the mapper treats attr as absent.
jordan: pinging devops — did the KMS key rotate or change policy last night?
devops: I rolled a key rotation script at 02:00 that rolled the key alias to a new CMK id (intended). Key policy should be identical. KMS metrics show elevated latency 02:01–02:06; console says throttling spikes to 20 req/s for alias/xxx.
sec-ops: is it possible the key policy denies decrypt from the auth-service principal after rotation? that would return AccessDenied not timeout, right?
alex: the stack shows `kms:DecryptTimeout` specifically. Possible root causes: cross-region calls, KMS throttling, or the envelope-decrypt loop blocking in our lambda.
okta-bot: automated: SAML assertion received for user bob@example.com. mapping outcome: roles=[guest]. reason=missing department attr.
sec-ops: we should confirm whether this is a runtime latency/throttling issue or a code-path bug that swallows decrypt errors and treats them as absent attrs.
olivia: agreed — immediate ask: can we restore the previous behavior (no KMS-encrypted attr) or force fallback to cached department on missing decrypt to avoid admin loss?
jordan: quick mitigation options:
- revert PR #4821 (roll back SAML attribute encryption)
- update role-mapper to treat decrypt errors as "temporary_failure" and fallback to last-known value in audit cache
- add explicit 500 on JIT so login fails loudly instead of assigning guest

devops: rollback would be fastest but requires coordination with oncall for downtime window. Role-mapper change is safer long-term.
sec-ops: audit question: how many privilege changes did this cause? we need a list of affected users and audit events for compliance.
alex: query run against audit-log-service shows ~112 users had role change from admin->guest between 02:03 and 02:08. I can export CSV.
sre_oncall: forensics — check whether any of those accounts did privileged actions after demotion (should be no).
okta-bot: note: recent Okta mapping rule now requires `department` for admin assignment. Rule id: rule-7-admin-dept.
olivia: sounds like two issues combined: policy change (require department) + attr decrypt failure. We should treat this as an incident.
sec-ops: incident classification: Sev2 (privilege regression affecting multiple users). Start timeline and mitigation.
jordan: immediate mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable rule-7-admin-dept in Okta (stop new demotions) 2) patch role-mapper to not assign guest on decrypt errors (roll forward) 3) investigate KMS latency root cause.
devops: I'll disable the Okta rule now. deploying change. deploy-bot: deploy 2026-02-14T02:21:45Z okta-config rollback rule-7-admin-dept by devops (initiated).
deploy-bot: success: okta rule disabled.
alex: once rule disabled, JIT will keep previous role if mapping not applicable? we still need to ensure we don't silently demote on decrypt timeout.
olivia: patch ready — small change to role-mapper to treat `kms:DecryptTimeout` as transient and requeue assertion for 3s; if still failing, escalate to 500 and log full audit. patch PR #4890.
jordan: timeline: deploy patch to staging ASAP, apply to prod if green.
sec-ops: collect audit log export and user notification draft. Compliance needs list + timeline + root cause analysis.
alex: also check KMS CloudWatch for region failovers; I see a brief control-plane blip in us-west-2 at 02:02 that correlated with higher latency. Could be transient AWS issue.
devops: opened AWS support ticket 1234567890 for KMS anomalies.
sre_oncall: action items summary: 
- devops: confirm KMS key policy and rotate back if necessary (ETA 1h)
- jordan+alex: deploy role-mapper patch (PR #4890) and run smoke tests (ETA 30m)
- olivia+sec-ops: export affected user list & notify stakeholders (ETA 1h)
- sec-ops: prepare compliance incident packet (ETA 3h)

olivia: one more ask — add a unit test that simulates KMS timeout and asserts we don't assign guest silently. Add to `auth-service/tests/role_mapper_test.go`.
alex: will do.
sec-ops: low-level note for RCA: we made an RBAC refactor (require department) + introduced KMS-encrypted attr without hardening error handling. Root cause = incomplete failure-mode handling. Remediation: change mapper semantics, improve observability (per-attr decrypt metrics), and add a fail-open vs fail-closed decision doc.
olivia: thanks all. keeping this thread updated. I'll post the CSV and timeline once I have it. :white_check_mark:
